fixes: In Tables, check the table's columns and choose again.
whys: These columns have a masking rule but are not in their table, so the rule does nothing: {columns}. The column was renamed or dropped after the rule was made; if it was renamed, the new name is sent as it is.
BeziSync could not read the tables' columns, so it could not check which ones hold personal data.

fixes: In Tables, choose Mask or Remove for each listed column, or Keep as is when it may be sent.
whys: These columns look like personal data and are sent as they are: {columns}. Their names suggest personal data (email, phone, address, birth date, card or ID numbers), and nobody chose what to do with them yet.
Tables added to a running pipeline are copied with an incremental snapshot; Vitess and Spanner have none, so such tables stream only their new changes.

fixes: Move the pipeline to Debezium 3.7.0 or newer (Change → Debezium version).
whys: Some sources need a recent Debezium Server: CockroachDB's sinkless changefeed arrived in Debezium 3.7. Blocks for an older official image; warns for a custom image whose release BeziSync can't read.

fixes: Upgrade the agent to BeziSync 0.3.0 or later (Settings → Runtimes shows the install command).

- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: [configmaps, secrets, services]

Pick key columns for these tables in the Transform step (Primary key), or add a primary key in the database.

whys: PostgreSQL logs the old row of an update only with REPLICA IDENTITY FULL. It makes the WAL larger for these tables.
fixes: ALTER TABLE "{schema}"."{table}" REPLICA IDENTITY FULL;
Drop replication slots nobody uses, or raise max_replication_slots and max_wal_senders (a restart).
whys: While a Flink CDC pipeline copies a PostgreSQL source, each of its readers opens its own temporary replication slot (and WAL sender) next to the pipeline's own one, so a copy needs 1 + parallelism of each. Without enough, the copy stops part-way.

fixes: Create this pipeline again: a new pipeline gets other server ids.

whys: A custom Flink CDC cluster is packed into TaskManagers the runtime's largest node can hold. When even one slot needs more CPU or memory than that node offers, or a manual TaskManager is bigger than it, its pods would never be scheduled. When the runtime doesn't report its nodes' size, BeziSync can't check and says so.
fixes: Give each slot less CPU or memory in Review → Size, or add bigger nodes to the runtime.
Use the automatic shape, or smaller TaskManagers, in Review → Size.

whys: A Flink CDC pipeline's saved position holds what each of its readers had read, so it restores only with the same number of readers. After Start over nothing is left to restore and the number can change.
fixes: Keep the readers it runs, or pause the pipeline and use Positions → Start over, then deploy.
